title: API versioning (URL, header, and query strategies)
hook: Public APIs outlive mobile apps and partner integrations — versioning lets you ship breaking changes without silently breaking clients. ASP.NET Core supports version in the URL path, a header, or a query parameter; each choice has caching, gateway, and developer-experience tradeoffs.

blocks.text: API versioning assigns a label (1.0, 2.0, or a date like 2024-06-01) to a contract snapshot. Clients pin to a version until they migrate. The Asp.Versioning.Mvc package adds [ApiVersion], versioned route templates, and sunset headers. Breaking changes include removing fields, renaming properties, changing status codes, or altering URL shapes. Non-breaking additions (new optional fields) usually do not require a new major version.

entries.plainDefinition: A change that causes existing clients to fail without modification — removing a field, changing types, renaming routes.
entries.example: v1 returns amount as string; v2 returns amount as decimal

entries.plainDefinition: Version embedded in the path segment — /api/v2/orders.
Client sends api-version: 2.0 or Accept header with version media type.
Signals when an old version will be retired so clients can plan migration.

blocks.text: Without versioning, your only options are never breaking changes (impossible long-term) or breaking clients on deploy. Versioning plus deprecation policy is how Stripe, GitHub, and Microsoft Graph ship evolution. Wrong strategy — query-string versions break CDN caches; header-only versions are invisible in browser devtools URL bars.

blocks.title: Default version policy
blocks.body: When a client omits a version, assume the oldest supported version or return 400 — document the choice. Silently routing to latest breaks clients when you ship v3.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Register versioning services
items.body: AddApiVersioning with readers for URL, header, and query; set default and report versions.

items.title: Mark controllers or minimal groups
items.body: [ApiVersion(1.0)] and [ApiVersion(2.0)] on separate types or methods.

items.title: Document both in OpenAPI
items.body: Swagger UI shows v1 and v2 documents or a single doc with version selector.

items.title: Deprecate v1
items.body: Add [Obsolete] metadata, Sunset header, and metrics on v1 traffic before removal.

diagram.title: Version resolution flow
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  R[Incoming request] --> U{URL contains v2?}
  U -->|Yes| V2[Route to v2 handlers]
  U -->|No| H{api-version header?}
  H -->|2.0| V2
  H -->|1.0 or missing| V1[Route to v1 handlers]
  V1 --> M[Deprecation middleware adds Sunset warning]

snippet.label: Register Asp.Versioning
snippet.explanation: Combine readers for flexibility — public partners may use URL versioning while mobile apps send a header. ReportApiVersions echoes supported versions in response headers.

snippet.label: Versioned controllers — breaking DTO change
snippet.explanation: v2 replaces string status with an enum and adds a timestamp — breaking for strict clients. Separate controllers keep v1 frozen while v2 evolves.

snippet.label: Minimal API versioned groups
snippet.explanation: v1 returns total as string (legacy); v2 returns decimal plus currency. Same route template, different handlers per version.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Versioning every endpoint when additive changes suffice. Using query-string version on cacheable GETs — CDNs ignore query strings inconsistently. Removing v1 without measuring traffic — breaks long-tail integrations. Mixing URL v2 with unversioned legacy routes in the same API surface.

blocks.text: Senior depth on versioning tradeoffs: URL versioning is visible, cache-friendly per path, and easy in API gateways — but pollutes REST purity and duplicates route tables. Header versioning keeps URLs clean and works for hypermedia — but harder to test in a browser address bar and easy to forget in HttpClient calls. Media-type versioning (Accept: application/vnd.company.v2+json) is precise but painful for tooling. Date-based versions (Stripe style) communicate sunset timelines clearly. In production, log api-version per request in App Insights; block v1 removal until traffic < 0.1% for two release cycles. Pair with OpenAPI diff in CI to catch accidental breaking changes.

blocks.title: Versioning tradeoffs (senior)
rows: Invisible, easy to omit, cache key complexity
CDN/cache pitfalls, easy to strip by proxies
Cannot fix past mistakes; field removal blocked
Different toolchain; breaking changes are subtle

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'we just deploy breaking changes and fix clients' on a public API question. Recommending query-string versioning for a CDN-fronted catalog without mentioning cache keys. Not having a deprecation plan — Sunset headers, metrics, and comms channels for partners.

interviewTakeaways: Version when you make breaking contract changes — not for every new optional field.
URL versioning is gateway- and cache-friendly; header versioning keeps URLs clean but is easier to forget.
Measure v1 traffic before removal; use Sunset headers and OpenAPI diff in CI.

60s: Pin clients to a version. URL for visibility, header for clean paths, avoid query for cacheable GETs. Ship v2 alongside v1. Deprecate with metrics. Breaking = remove/rename/type-change; additive fields are usually safe.
Follow-up: how would you version minimal APIs vs controllers in the same service?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'latest version when unspecified' gets you rejected — silent upgrades break clients on your next deploy.
Query-string versioning on GET catalog endpoints breaks CDN caching without custom cache keys.
Strong answer: 'URL for public partners, header for mobile, default 1.0 with ReportApiVersions, Sunset before removal, OpenAPI diff in CI.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: const v1 = express.Router(); app.use('/v1', v1) is the Express equivalent of URL segment versioning. No built-in header reader — you write middleware.
NestJS supports URI, header, and media-type versioning with @Version('2'). Conceptually mirrors Asp.Versioning attribute model.
